utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Lukic, the Chamber was informed that you'd like to raise a preliminary matter in open session. How much time would you need for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Two minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two minutes. Then we'll ask the usher to already be on stand by to escort the witness into the courtroom, but effective only after two minutes. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning, Your Honours. Your Honours raised a question of our expert pathologist, Mr. Stankovic, and I spoke with my colleague Mr. Ivetic who is more privy to the issue and he said that Mr. Stankovic was already appointed, that documentation was handed in, most of it to him, we still have to transfer some documents but he will most probably rely on the expertise of late Mr. Dunjic. But our intention is to bring Mr. Stankovic and to testify on that part of expertise. So since -- as I understood Mr. Ivetic, there are some things that should be added on -- and it was the plan with Mr. Dunjic that something has to be explained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One of our concerns was timing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We are aware of your concern. I spoke with Mr. McCloskey. That was his big concern as well, and that's why the Prosecution is ready to be more lenient on admission of the expertise, but, still, we plan to bring Mr. Stankovic to testify on that issue as well, and we'll try to work with him to have his testimony as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As soon as possible is a very flexible concept.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He promised that his Tomasica report should be done soon. I think till the end of November. And I don't know how do we stand with the rest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, Mr. President. In my discussions with the Defence, the Prosecution had agreed that the testimony of Dr. Dunjic from Karadzic could come in, his report could come in, and that would give -- we thought was hoping what they needed for the Srebrenica side of things, and Dr. Stankovic, I guess, has always been scheduled for Tomasica. Stankovic using the Dunjic report would be unusual. I'll need to discuss that with the team and get our position on that. Though taking any amount of time to do a new report would really be problematic especially since there is this product from Dr. Dunjic who has been on this Srebrenica case for a long time and has provided multiple reports. So we'll continue to discuss this, though. It shouldn't take us very long and try to encourage the Defence to be able to get this done hopefully before the year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see there's a lot of discussion, there's a lot of problems, et cetera. Could you provide the Chamber by the beginning of next week with a more concrete plan on how to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the witness may be escorted in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Kijac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I -- my first request would be to speak up a little bit and to come a bit closer to the microphone. And I further like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony, that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 33182.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a document you sent as deputy prime minister -- and we're waiting for the B/C/S. It's a document you sent as deputy prime minister on the 24th of December, 1997 to the chief of the VRS General Staff at the time, the minister of the interior and the chairman of the state commission for the exchange of prisoners of war and missing persons. We see in the first paragraph that you are mentioning: "The international community and the Muslim-Croatian side have lately intensified their activities relating to the exhumation of alleged mass graves in the territory of Republika Srpska and carried out other activities aimed at achieving political and security-related effects against our republic." We see you're calling a joint meeting. And, at the end, we see you describing it as significant and important and direct that attendance is mandatory. So it was your position that the exhumation of possible mass graves in the Republika Srpska was a significant national security issue; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this was created on the basis of a letter from the state commission for the exchange of prisoners of war, so they wrote to me in order to convene a joint meeting, to agree on measures, if I can put it that way, related to the exhumation of alleged mass graves in the territory of Republika Srpska. So this document was created at the request of the state commission for the exchange of prisoners and missing persons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please answer the question, Witness. The question was not triggered this letter to be sent. The question was whether you considered the matter of national security concern.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It doesn't say that anywhere here. I don't see in which paragraph there's a reference to that or that Mr. Traldi mentioned it. If I can see it well, there's no mention of that. If that is not the case, please help me find it, national security. This refers to joint activities of the army, the Ministry of Interior, and the state commission for the exchange of prisoners of war in order to harmonise procedures and agree on measures in that direction. I don't see any reference to national security. Now, whether I'm right or not --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... first, do you see at the end of the first paragraph where you say that the exhumation of graves is in your judgement aimed at achieving political and security-related effects against what you describe as "our republic"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Political security-related, yes; but not national security. And there's a reference to alleged mass graves. So we're not saying mass graves. Alleged mass graves. In the territory of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 33237.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you not insisting on an answer to your question? Your question has still not been answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, did you or did you not consider the exhumation of alleged mass graves, as we see in the document, to be a national security issue?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not national security. Again, I am talking about political security-related effects and possible propaganda. Because, at that time, we did not know what kind of graves were involved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I may draw your attention to the fact that it is not political security but political and security-related effects. Would that change your position, your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, no, I don't see it here. This is a joint meeting in order to have measures taken because at that time there's lots of propaganda. We still do not have - how I do put this? - we do not know the proportions of the graves. We don't have identified persons or exhumations --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... would you please answer my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: First paragraph last sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's in English only, and we can find only in English, not in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The witness could have answered that but he addressed another matter. In English, it says: "Aimed at achieving political and security-related effects ..." Do you see the similar formulation in the first paragraph, Mr. Kijac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do. In all fairness in the Serbian version it's a bit different. But that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: How is it --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The translation is not exactly the way you had put it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Then please read the end of the last sentence of paragraph 1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "As well as other activities calculated at achieving political security-related effects against our republic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, could you take care of a revised translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We will. Can we have 65 ter 33237, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we see the B/C/S on the screen already. You mentioned your document was issued in response to a document coming from the exchange commission. We see this one is sent on 2nd of December, 1997, that it's sent to the president of the Assembly, Mr. Kalinic, to you, and to General Colic at the Main Staff. We see a handwritten note at the top right to call a meeting. Do you recognise that handwriting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This precedes the paper that you showed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And whose handwriting is it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to page 3 in both languages, we read in the last paragraph that the gentleman sending you the letter considers there to be exceptional security and political significance and potential detrimental consequences to realising the stated activities of the opposing sides. And if we turn back to page 2, in both languages, we see a reference, second paragraph in the English, to naming exhumation priorities in the municipality of Nevesinje and we see just a little bit lower down that someone has been identified who can -- who the exchange commission thinks could provide information, a survivor, Jasminka Ploskic, who was held captive. Now in that context can we have 65 ter 33253. Now, this is a document coming from the Mostar sector of the Bosnian committee for missing persons, dated 8 October 2007. We read at the top -- top of the text so just below the subject line, that Republika Srpska military and paramilitary units had captured group of 76 Bosniak civilians at Jasenovo Do on the 26th of June, 1992 while running away; 20 children, 27 men, 26 women, the youngest child being only seven days old. Turning to page 3 in both languages, we read at the bottom of the page in the English and near the top in the B/C/S that three prisoners from the group survived. The first name being Ms. Ploskic's again and all three being women. Turning to page 5 in English, 4 in B/C/S, we see that as of 2007, 42 persons had still not been found. So my question for you is, sir, why was the fate of these people so secret that it required a meeting of the highest levels of the military, political and police institutions in the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, this federal list of the commission for missing persons, there is the first time I see it. Secondly, Mr. Rosic, in the document that you showed me a moment ago, could you please have it returned? He is asking to have a meeting convened in order to agree on activities. And on the basis of this letter sent by Mr. Rosic, who chaired the commission for exchanges at that point, I think so, later on he was a judge of our constitutional Court so he asked for such a meeting at top level. There's no reference to prevention, but just to determining all relevant elements regarding the situation these requests of the commissions for exchanges of prisoners of war. It was probably a joint commission of the Muslim, Croat and Serb sides, and they proposed certain measures at certain locations. As for this meeting that I convened, there's nothing there except saying what kind of logistical support we can provide, what kind of security measures and so on. Because at the time --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... sorry, at the time? Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you interrupted me. You interrupted my train of thought. It's hard for me to think of what it was that I was trying to say then. So, the meeting was convened at the initiative of the chairman of the commission for exchange of prisoners of war, Mr. Rosic. That can be seen from the previous document that you showed me. He mentions certain locations. As for this third document, this is the first time I see it. That is to say I was not involved in the exchange of prisoners of war. We, in the Ministry of Interior, were supposed to secure certain locations, physically, where this was requested --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We didn't hear the end of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, before I move on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can I ask you one question. When I read through that letter from the federal committee for missing persons, there is concern that one might find out. That's what that letter includes, isn't it? They may be aware of the micro-locations. They even -- they make it public, not, Let's assist those people in finding their deceased loved ones, and let's secure the locations and give our assistance. The gist of it is difficult to understand as you understand it, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I haven't read this letter. I don't know who this letter was sent to. The sector of Mostar, no, was it sent to the commission of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... sir, I think you've misunderstood the Judge' question, he is speaking of the letter that was sent to you that bore your handwriting in the top corner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's -- it may be helpful to have that one on the screen again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 33237.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's the letter I think you said triggered writing your letter. You said, although not asked, I wrote that letter because I had received another letter. Now, if I look at this letter of the federal committee for missing persons, where we find your handwriting on top of it, that is not a letter, Would you please assist with securing the exhumations and make it all safe and secure, it is -- they're at a point not only to know where the mass graves are, micro-locations, but also they are going to make that public. They want public exposure. They want a public interview with one of the persons and that's not exactly what you told us, is this letter or this action is about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mean, I don't know how to explain this to you, Your Honour. I am a co-ordinator only. I never worked in the commission for prisoners of war and missing persons. So in order to have something done there, the Ministry of the Interior and the army have to be called -- I mean, I don't know anything about graves. Absolutely nothing. I am deputy prime minister, co-ordinating the work of the army and police, and nothing else. And that is why I convened this meeting at the initiative of Mr. Rosic, so that they would say what it is that was supposed to be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you are giving us a picture that your assistance is requested so that everything could be secured, that everything would be safe, and that is not the language we find either in this letter nor in the letter in which you invite others to participate. But I leave to that. If you say that's your explanation, then it's your explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender the last three documents, 65 ter 33182, 33237, and 33253.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, in the same sequence, the numbers assigned would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P7655, P7656, and P7657, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7655 up to and including P7657 are admitted into evidence, but with the caveat that one of them needs a revised translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And that's the first one, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, you were -- I think Mr. Traldi started tendering the documents when I gave you an opportunity to give any brief further comment. If you have given your explanation and if there's no wish to add anything to that, we'll proceed; otherwise, we'd like to hear what you'd like to add.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I have nothing to add. I mean, Your Honour. I told you what this is all about and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... if you have nothing to add, then we'll proceed. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P1586.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now we see here a document you forwarded on the 16th of January, 1996 enclosing the text of a dispatch from the Main Staff sector for intelligence and security sent to the MUP, and the dispatch had requested, inter alia, that the minister - at the time you - order the Bijeljina MUP to issue IDs with Serbian first and last names to a group of the 10th Sabotage Detachment. We see if we zoom in at the bottom of the page in the English and the middle of the page in the B/C/S, that these are identified as "foreign citizens or on a list of individuals who have been indicted by The Hague Tribunal." Now, turning to page 2 in the English and at the bottom of page one in the B/C/S, we read: "You are required to act on the request by the GS VRS." And then below that, we see: Minister Dragan Kijac. So you ordered your subordinates, pursuant to this document sent you by the Main Staff, to issue fake IDs to people indicted by this Tribunal; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's completely all right, considering that there is an instruction to have co-operation between security and intelligence services and the ministry. The intelligence service can, at any time, request surveillance, checking of correspondence and communication of any person at any time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... sir, I hadn't asked you for a list of the powers or responsibilities of the intelligence service. I'd asked you what we see here is you ordering your subordinates to issue fake IDs to VRS soldiers thought to be indicted by The Hague Tribunal. That's what we see here; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think he answered that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Traldi, in the legal system of Republika Srpska, at that time, the Tribunal did not exist. We had our laws at the time. I believe co-operation with the ICTY was adopted only in 2001. In 1996, I had absolutely no obligation to co-operate with The Hague Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... can we see P1677?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now this is an authorisation by General Mladic for travel to the FRY dated the 11th of February, 1996 sent to the MUP. We see three names, and the first is Drazen Erdemovic. These are three of the people who had been issued -- well, let's put it this way: He is one of the people who was issued a fake ID, pursuant to your order; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, I got away from the microphone. As a rule when new identities are created, one doesn't know for whom. That's to say, Mr. Salapura did not write me a list of persons for whom new IDs are needed. He just gave me a list of eight persons and said false identities have to be created. False identities were created very frequently. You have thousands of books describing how intelligence agents travelled abroad with false identities, so you have the Presidency of the SFRY --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... sir, I'm not interested in a literature review. How common was it that you created false identities for people thought to be indicted by The Hague Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, at that time, The Hague Tribunal did not exist, as far as I'm concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Second, I did not know who these persons were. It was not the practice to communicate to me their identities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You could read in the document that they were thought to be indicted by the Tribunal. The practice allowed you to do that; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Practice is one thing. However, this request of the military intelligence service is one which does not have to state the reason. They can even --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you're again --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- deceive me --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you're again, stating points of doctrine that don't respond to the question. Is it your evidence that you somehow missed that the request sent to you, that you forwarded to your subordinates in its entirety, referred to these as people thought to be indicted by The Hague Tribunal. Did you somehow miss that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the list of those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nowhere in that dispatch do I see who they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 33196a.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for that. Witness, I have the following question for you: You said well, the Tribunal didn't exist for us. We were not under an obligation to co-operate. Now, whether that's true or not, I just leave that apart. But, here, this looks as if it is a small operation which is frustrating and obstructing the work of the Tribunal. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From that point of view, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you actively participated in an effort to obstruct and frustrate the work of this Tribunal by sending -- by this correspondence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I only sent a letter, if I had wanted to hide something, if I had no authority to do this, I could have made only a phone call. You have to understand that at that time I was acting in accordance with the laws of Republika Srpska and the laws governing security.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The laws, if I understand the meaning of what a law is, never say, Do this or do that. They give powers, and by the use of those powers - and that's what I'm asking you about - you actively participated in an evident to obstruct and frustrate the work of this Tribunal. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm telling you again, that I had absolutely no information which people are concerned. The letter doesn't say it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I -- I leave it to that. I mean whether it's Mr. A, B, and C or X, Y, and Z who were given fake IDs is not relevant if Mr. A, B and C and Mr. X, Y and Z are defined as persons who were on a list of individuals who have been indicted. I leave it to that. Mr. Traldi please proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have the bottom of this page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is a portion of testimony by the Omarska commander Zeljko Mejakic in his own trial in Bosnia and he is asked, "How did you go to Serbia?" He says, "I simply sat on a bus and used a forged identity card issued to me by the people there. Actually, it was not a forged identity card in terms of the authenticity of the document itself and the stamp. The Ministry of Interior gave me an identity card with a different name, and with this identify card I crossed into Serbia and stayed there until I surrendered to the Tribunal. Was Mr. Mejakic -- Mr. Mejakic was also one of the fugitives who got a false ID from the MUP to avoid arrest by the Tribunal; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm hearing for the first time about Mr. Mejakic. I have no idea who he is. I don't see that passage that you've read out, Mr. Traldi. I would like to see it. If you can highlight it here, but I don't know anything about Mr. Mejakic. Who is he? Is that the group?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's at the bottom part in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You see the words "MUP" at the very end, and if we turn to the top of the next page, you see him explain crossing into Serbia.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "How did you go to Serbia?" Is that the beginning of the passage? It's the one paragraph before last.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... we need the top of the next page to get his explanation of crossing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it's for context it's good that the witness reads the last few lines of the previous page in which he, indeed, explains how he travelled using a forged identity card. But could we go to the bottom of that page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Of the previous page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please read the part from where you said -- it's the three, four last lines. And once you've done, please tell us so that we can move to the next page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can move to the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First two lines is what you're supposed to read.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've read it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Two follow-up questions, if we can have the previous page in B/C/S back. As we get it, yesterday you repeated to this Court as fact evidence, you said you'd heard from other witnesses in other trials. If you follow the trials at the ICTY, how could it possibly be true that you have no idea who the Omarska camp commander is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't follow trials, Mr. Traldi. I would have time to -- I wouldn't have time to do anything in my life if I followed trials. But I just happened to read something, one part of one trial. If I had been following trials, I wouldn't have been able to do my normal job from 8.00 to 4.00 p.m. every day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you keep your answers short. Who provided you with the portion you did read?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe I've read it, maybe I've seen it. I could have seen one bit of something. But I'm at work from 8.00 to 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question is: Who gave it to you? You said you read a certain portion. You happened to have read --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot remember that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's an answer to my question. Mr. Traldi. Could you please keep your answers short and just tell us what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, looking about halfway down the page in the B/C/S, Mr. Mejakic is asked how he left the police force and when and for what reason. He answers: "In November 1996, simply put, in 1996, the then-minister of the interior, Kijac, Dragan Kijac, told me through the then-chief of the Security Services Centre, Ranko Mijic, to leave the service and stay away." How could you have relayed this message to him if you did not know who he was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many people were terminated in 1996. I would like to see the report. But I believe we terminated around 500 or over 500 employees for different reasons. I don't have that report with me. I would like to have it. But in 1996, a large number of people were let go. I would not like to speculate now, but I think the figure could be as high as 500 because that is the year --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you are expounding on matters which are not in the question. I do understand that without consulting documents, you have no recollection about this individual case. That's how I understand your answer. Mr. Traldi, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 33179.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You mentioned people dismissed in 1996. As we see here, one of the people that you appointed to the MUP in 1996 assigned as your advisor was Simo Drljaca, the wartime chief of the Prijedor SJB and Mejakic's boss; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that. It's true. I see this, a decision concerning Simo Drljaca; that is, that he is dismissed at -- as the chief of the Prijedor public security centre and appointed advisor to the Ministry of Interior of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I tender the document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 33179 receives exhibit number P7658, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, can we have 65 ter 33255.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As it comes up, we saw one of the people General Mladic was telling your MUP to let cross the border was Drazen Erdemovic. This is an article from 22 March 1996, titled: "I killed 'only' hundreds of people." Looking at the third paragraph of the text, we see Erdemovic, we see his name in the second and fourth paragraphs. We see he said that at a place referred to as Pilice farm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the portion in B/C/S be enlarged which is relevant for the --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's below the words, "It was shot in the heads."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but in the B/C/S those words do not appear. Yes. A little bit to the left. Further to -- no, that's to the right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the portion you read, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see a reference to place called Pilice Farm. We see a reference to a lieutenant-colonel explaining the task, that a bus with Muslim civilians, men who should be liquidated. Below that we read, "Killing commenced immediately. Civilians in groups of tens were taken out of the buses and were taken to the field." We read --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please wait a moment. It has to be enlarged again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: At the top of the second column in the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We read that Erdemovic thinks he killed between 70 to 100 people himself and estimates the full number of killed as close to 1200. We discussed when you acquired information about the genocide at Srebrenica last time you were here. You would have noticed this article; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I don't even see when --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- this article was written. I've never read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm now going to ask Ms. Stewart to show a video 65 ter 33270a. The transcript has been confirmed so we can play it only once.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, do you have any information about date of the publication of this document you just showed us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I believe I'd put it on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I missed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As 22nd of March, 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I should have said that the name of the newspaper is Slobodna Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: "THE INTERPRETER: [Voiceover] "Reporter: Immediately upon her arrival in Sarajevo, Madeleine Albright held a press conference at the American embassy which focussed on the work of the Hague Tribunal, and the visit to a mass grave near Janja. She said that this was an important step that provides evidence of systematic killing of about 1.000 people and that this place is also different from other places because ... "Madeleine Albright: [In English] ... we actually have evidence supplied by the killers themselves and corroborating the story that we saw. I was able to take with me on this trip investigators from the war crimes Tribunal so that ... and they were able to explain to me what they were seeing and were preparing their work. "THE INTERPRETER: [Voiceover] "Reporter: 'Peace can be reached only if all the perpetrators are punished, both collectively and individually.' Madeleine Albright says she does not believe the entire people to be responsible for the crimes but she thinks that is something that people from this region have to face. "Madeleine Albright: [In English] It is very difficult to deal with the fact that scores of people must have known what was going on and that this kind of barbarism took place in this area is disgusting. "THE INTERPRETER: [Voiceover] "Reporter: After the formal meetings, Ambassador Albright was welcomed at Dom Ljiljana by the US ambassador in our country, John Menzies, after which the esteemed guest gave an inspired speech about Bosnia in the time of war, Bosnia today and Bosnia in the future. Early on during her first visit to Sarajevo when she came to set the cornerstone of the US embassy, Albright expressed her country's political viewpoint regarding our country, speaking about Sarajevo as an undivided capital. 'Even though there was a lot of scepticism, the people of Sarajevo proved that the opposite was true.'"

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think for efficiency we've seen the part we need.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we are at 2:16.6, where we stopped looking at the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Did you also miss Albright's press conference in Bosnia about this mass grave?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm seeing this report for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P348, page 47.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, again you see this now for the first time. Did you not know that such a press conference was given at all, I mean, apart from whether you looked at this or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I knew that Madeleine Albright made a visit to Bosnia-Herzegovina and that she visited someplace along the Drina. I don't know exactly where. Security was provided by our State Security Service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you didn't know that that was a place which was considered to be a mass grave and that she was accompanied by investigators of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must tell you that I learned that later. Much later. I stopped being minister of the interior in mid-1997, and in the beginning of 1998, I was already living in Serbia. So from 1997, I've had absolutely nothing to do and no powers within the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So a non-evasive answer to the question that was earlier put to you by Mr. Traldi would have been: I missed it at the time, but I learned about it later. Where he asked whether you missed Albright's press conference in Bosnia about this mass grave. You learned about her visit and all that later and not when you provided security for her visit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you see, I see from this press conference that it was broadcast by the Radio Television Bosnia-Herzegovina. It's a big question what was transmitted by the Radio Television of Republika Srpska. You have to understand at that time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... witness, you're evading my question. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I apologise for my own ambiguity in calling the document up, or error. Can we have page 44 and I'm asking for the B/C/S original rather than the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that page 44 of P348.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Of P348.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we have the correct English page because I had not made an error that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, we see here an entry in General Mladic's notebook for a meeting with Karadzic on 22nd March 1996, the same date as the Slobodna Bosna article. We see he records Karadzic as saying: "A big show was put on for Albright. She expected they would find 1200 Muslim bodies at Pilica but they found some five bodies." Now, 1200, that's the same number of bodies that's referred to in the Slobodna Bosna article; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, we see the fourth bullet, someone named Fico was here last night and he says that those two would sell the story about Srebrenica to The Hague. You remember you confirmed last time that Frenki Simatovic had a deputy named Dragan Filipovic, also known as Fico; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you remember that he had such a deputy or do you just fail to remember that you confirmed it when you were testifying last month?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the answer is yes ... I don't see what the context is. Fico can be this Fico or that Fico. It is correct that he had a co-worker whose nickname was Fico. I cannot remember the name now but I think it was Filipovic, Fico, or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And looking above that, if we can zoom in on the third hyphen, we see a name. The first name is Dragisa and the last name is a little bit difficult to read in the original. Can you help us with that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very hard for me to read this text, but I'll make an effort. I can't read it. Could you please try to read it for me, if you have the text? I really cannot. He will ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It starts in the English that Dragisa, and in English, it's translated as: "Milic will come and he will show a cassette about her visit ... we will see it ..." Now, you had a deputy named Dragisa Mihic; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it Mihic or Milic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The deputy is Mihic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mihic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mihic, I don't see the date. It's the 28th of March, 1993, is it, Mr. Traldi? I can't see the date up here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... sir, the 22nd of March, 1996. Same date as the Slobodna Bosna article; reference to the Albright press conference we just saw.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see here the 22nd of March, but I don't see exactly which year. So 1996? Well, at that time, Dragisa Mihic was not my deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What was his position at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, in 1996, Dragisa Mihic was head of the state security sector. He was not deputy minister of the interior. He was head of the state security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see the time. I'd tender the two documents I used on this topic, 65 ter 33255, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's number one. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives Exhibit number P7659, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And 33270a, the video.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives exhibit number P7660.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted. Yes, and it's time for a break. It's already beyond the time. Witness, would you please follow the usher. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, about time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I was about to address that, Your Honour. Though it's been a little bit more difficult than usual to anticipate time with this witness, I do have one very brief topic to deal with. I wouldn't think it would be more than ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break, and we'll resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just for ease of reference in the record, Your Honours, I'm told the image at 1:1.7 seconds in the video just admitted, which is P7660, appears -- or a very similar image appears at P7267. And while the witness comes, in for efficiency, if we could have P4234.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the number, Mr. Traldi. I think I heard P4234 but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You did. And my speed of speech must have been off, but it is 4234 that I'd asked for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, finally and briefly, I want to return to your evidence about the Milos group. Now this is a proposal to the RS MUP, attention the deputy secretary of the SNB, sent on the 20th of October, 1993. At that time this proposal would have gone to you; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer. We didn't receive interpretation because you were not close to the microphone, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it was sent to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And in the second paragraph, we read: "In July 1991," and this is a proposal for promotion and decoration for Predrag Radulovic. We read: "In July 1991, he was appointed before the Banja Luka SNB sector as a liaison officer for the contact with the MUP Serbia." So you knew that Mr. Radulovic, who you discussed last time, was responsible for liaising with MUP Serbia; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what this letter says.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 33289.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the question was whether you knew that. You are not invited to tell us what the letter says because we can read that but -- therefore, you did know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. In June 1991, I worked at the Banja Luka Security Services Centre, and I did not have any duties in the state security.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, again, the question is not whether you were in a position where you should have known or could have known. The question is whether - and this letter is presented to you which makes it very likely - that you knew about this appointment and this position of Predrag Radulovic. Did you know that or did you not know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You received the letter in which that is stated, but you did not read it or you did not ... what made it that this letter which you said would reach your desk or your office, that that information didn't come through.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to take a look at the second page as well, if possible, Your Honour, where the text continues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're not here to interpret letters. You're here to answer questions. Did you know --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I just need to read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Whether you know it or not is your own recollection. If you say, I don't remember, then perhaps it may be that, looking further at the document may refresh your recollection. But did you know or did you not know that he was appointed as -- to liaise with the MUP Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 33289. And it's only in B/C/S at the moment. So if we could zoom in on point 1. This is a document dated 29 July 1994 and coming from Nedjelko Kesic, the head of the -- by then the RDB in Banja Luka. At point 1 we see that Mr. Radulovic is put in charge of line 2 of the RDB in Banja Luka; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did not approve this reassignment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This was not the question. Please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please repeat the question again.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could all other microphones please be switched off when the witness is speaking. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could you just read for us beginning at the word "Radulovic" and ending with the semi-colon, before the number 2.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Radulovic Predrag, to the position of head of department O 2 in the centre of the RDB Banja Luka." If that's the paragraph you had in mind. May I proceed, Mr. Traldi?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, you should wait for a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What we see here is Mr. Kesic recommending him for a promotion; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But, Mr. Traldi, do allow me to continue. Just two sentences. This was done by the minister of the interior of Republika Srpska. This is his request sent to me. As far as I can remember, I did not approve this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is to say --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Mr. Kesic, who worked with Radulovic, seems to think he was doing a pretty good job; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was probably his opinion, but this was the opinion and position of the minister of the interior. And this was explicitly done at the proposal of the minister of the interior. You see that it's the minister's office there, and what is sent to me is a request --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... witness, you've answered the question by the first one line. Stop discussing the whole of the document to -- just limit yourself to answer the question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 33314.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is one of the Milos documents dated 5th of August, 1992 that says: "We've been asked by the chief of the Banja Luka SNB to urge through you that the agreed help in technical equipment be provided." Now, what we see here is the Milos group relaying a request from SNB Banja Luka to MUP Serbia, consistent with their role as a liaison; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I see what it is that the Milos group is asking for. However, there is not going through the under-secretary. This does not go through the state security sector. For five times now I have told you and I've pointed out that they were not allowed to communicate with other services. The service of Serbia, the service the Montenegro, without the agreement of the head of the sector. So they did this incognito. I am not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So when Mr. Kesic wrote to you in October 1993 and said, Promote Predrag Radulovic because I appointed him liaison with MUP Serbia, did you fire Kesic for appointing a liaison rather than going through you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not exactly that the situation was like that. It's not that I just could have dismissed people. You have my document in which I'm responding to the Minister of the Interior that I do not want to act on his orders because I thought that at that moment that, as the head of the state security, I need to appoint people at my own discretion. You have that document. And that's not the only time when the minister tried on his own to promote certain people precisely for these reasons, and we did not allow that. And that's why, in 1994, I was replaced because I did not want to promote certain people to certain positions as had been suggested to me by the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P3211.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do that, I noticed that in this Milos document it specifically said that the activity was approved also by the minister of the MUP of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. You have read that? Any comment on this specific reference to this approval?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We supported that proposal, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is one of the Milos reports, this one from 30 April 1992. We see at the first sentence that it reports on the take-over of Prijedor on that date. Sir, you don't contest that this Milos report is accurate; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give any comment on this. I don't know about this. The Milos group never addressed the state security sector, and it can be seen that this document was not sent to us --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Sir. Sir.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and, at that time --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: All I asked you was: Do you or don't you contest the accuracy of this report, that the most important buildings in Prijedor were occupied and all roads leading to the town were blocked by armed formations of the Serbian people on 30 April 1992. You know that to be true; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that for you, Mr. Traldi. In April 1992 I was in Sarajevo. You know --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- Prijedor --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We do not understand what the witness is saying. We cannot hear him at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, again, even if you are in Sarajevo, you sometimes have knowledge of what happened elsewhere. The simple question is: Wherever you were, but you can confirm that these first two lines of this report reflect what actually happened.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, really, I cannot confirm that for you because I worked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... no, no -- the reasons why you can't confirm. You can't confirm. Leave it to that. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P6890. It will be another Milos report.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As it comes up, the Chamber has received evidence from Mr. Radulovic that he signed reports to MUP Serbia Milos but did not sign reports to the Republika Srpska national security sector that way. Would that explain why you don't recognise the format of the Milos reports?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I see this format. This kind of format could not have reached me. First of all, we have to look at the date. What is the date? It is only from August --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... sir, I'm going to be very quick with this document. This is the Milos report that Mr. Lukic showed you during direct examination. You have no explanation for how this report could have wound up in the DB Serbia archive, do you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, to the DB of the Republic of Serbia, but not the DB of Republika Srpska. Obviously it did arrive somewhere, but the archives that Republika Srpska had, no, this did not reach that. This kind of report would have to be addressed to someone. In our case, everybody would have to write up exactly who composed this, who drafted it, and so on, and pseudonyms could not be used for signatures. This is the first time I see this document. Actually, it was first shown to me in court and I don't see the date, and at that time I don't know whether I was head of the sector or whether it was the late Slobodan Skipina who was there. Because I came to head the sector only at the end of August, beginning of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, that completes my questions for this witness. I tender 65 ter 33314 and ask that 65 ter 33289 be marked for identification. 33314 being the Milos request that had been approved by the RS minister of the interior; and 33289 being Kesic's proposal to promote Radulovic in July 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, 33314 would receive number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P7661, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. 65 ter 33289.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives exhibit number P7662, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Marked for identification. Mr. Lukic, are you ready to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Give me one second, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Kijac.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You started a long time ago, so I will try to remind you of certain things.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have P7586 on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the document, I'm going to start explaining to you. This is the document where it says that you chaired the meeting on the 10th of November, 1993 and that on the 11th of November, the acting minister Tomo Kovac chaired the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we have pages 4 in both versions, please. And we'll need paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You explained that it wasn't possible for you to chair this session and that, indeed, you did not chair it. This is what I'd like to ask you: Was Tomo Kovac ever minister of the interior of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I can remember, acting minister, yes; minister, no. The document says "acting minister Tomo Kovac" as well, if I can see this paragraph well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, in relation to this chairmanship, could it happen sometimes that the collegium of the National Security Service would be chaired by someone from public security?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not even the minister. The collegium of the National Security Service is chaired by the head of the National Security Service or the head of the state security sector, irrespective of the presence of the minister or the deputy minister of the interior who were above them in terms of hierarchy. It could never happen that someone from public security even including the minister of the interior who was the highest in the hierarchy, no one like that could have chaired the meeting. So I couldn't have chaired it either. There are about ten assistant ministers here and I don't know anything about the fields that they deal with. Legal affairs, finance, and so on. So crime prevention as head of the state security sector, I'm not involved in that, or general administrative affairs, or police affairs or police -- I really do apologise to the interpreters. I get so carried away. And, in addition to that, as far as I know, the chiefs of public security are there, and they were not under the head of state security.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us look at P7577. We'll see on the screen that photograph showing people about whom you were asked if they shared the same goals. Do you recall it now?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then you were shown the following document. Could we see P7578. It's a document from the Ministry of Interior, the public security sector -- state security sector - correction - dated 5 July 1994, Belgrade, the Republic of Serbia. And below, it's written in the last sentence that was put to you: "We are now entering the decisive phase of the fight to achieve the common goals of all the Serbian lands ..." Before 1994 - so we are talking about 1991, 1992 - do you remember whether the Croatian and Muslim leadership received offers to remain in the joint, the common state?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war, yes. There was also the initiative of Adil Zulfikarpasic that Bosnia remain whole, and if I remember correctly an offer was made to them that Alija Izetbegovic become the president of the federal government and that Bosnia remain whole and part of the then-Yugoslavia, the so-called rump Yugoslavia as it was at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was the answer of Mr. Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Organising the referendum in which the Serbian people did not participate and proclamation of independence, which actually led to the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I should like to call up P7581. We will see a transcript of a video-clip where Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan, is speaking. On this page, only one sentence is left where Arkan says: "We don't take any more prisoners. We will kill every Fascist soldier we catch. They must know that." Below that, among the participants in the middle, there's a letter Z, and it says "captured Croatian soldier." So contrary to this claim, we see that one of the participants in this conversation is a captured Croatian soldier. What was the information available to your service? Did you know how Arkan treated prisoners?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, I said last time, and I said that in my statement, Arkan appeared in Bijeljina at the time when Bosnia-Herzegovina was united as a state. After that, he was no longer present in those lands until the fall of Krajina, and then occurred the misunderstanding and the strenuous demand of General Mladic that he withdraw, because he had taken upon himself to acted as military police. And as far as I know, at the demands of General Mladic, he left. He had been there for 15 or 20 days in the areas of Banja Luka and Sanski Most, but we did not deal with Raznjatovic at the time because we had different concerns. Our municipalities were falling, the regular Croatian army was entering the territory of the Republika Srpska together with the 5th Corps and within that month or month and a half, from August and September, nine or ten municipalities fell. Prijedor and Banja Luka were in danger and Arkan probably appeared to assist, as he saw it, the Serbian people. However, since I knew from before about the clear stance of General Mladic, namely that he did not allow any paramilitary organisation and as soon as the Army of Republika Srpska was established, he chased out across the Drina river all paramilitary units or placed them under his command. Because in those first two month, April and May, there were paramilitary units along the entire bank of the Drina, from Bratunac onwards. These were people who mostly came were Serbia who imposed themselves because the authorities were not functioning, and they created some independent paramilitary units which, in that vacuum before the army was established, became an important factor. And then there was the arrest of Yellow Wasps in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the witness is going to gave page-long speeches that go well beyond every question Mr. Lukic asks it creates risk -- and that raise new topics and at the end of the last answer, a new event that hadn't been discussed on cross-examination, it raises the possibilities of going into new areas on recross, and I just ask that Mr. Lukic exert some control.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I have another observation to make at this moment. Mr. Lukic, earlier you said that the presence of -- you -- first of all, you referred us to letter Z --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's the list of those who are present that appears in the B/C/S version; however, not in the English version so would you take care in order for English-speaking persons to be able to follow, to take care that that will be translated as well. Because it is only in B/C/S. Second, would you refrain from doing the job of the Chamber, because you said: So contrary to this claim, whether the presence of a Croatian soldier contradicts what Mr. Arkan said, that is, that they are going to kill every prisoner, is for the Chamber to determine, and certainly not something you should put to a witness. And I think, if Mr. Traldi would not have intervened, we soon would have done so. Long speeches; link with the question very weak, if at all. So would you please keep better control of the testimony of your witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Although this witness did answer my several following questions, but I will move on to the next topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kijac, you were asked last month if there were non-Serbs in the National Security Service, and you said there were none at Pale. You said that the people who joined the service were Serbs who managed to leave the city -- to get out of the city.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you give us a reference, Mr. Lukic, so that I can re-read that portion of the evidence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't have it with me. I don't know how it happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was it when he answered one of your questions or was it when he answered one of Mr. Traldi's questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi's questions. We'll find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did it ever happen that somebody applied to the National Security Service and was rejected if he was a Muslim or a Croat?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in Sarajevo? No. People even got out with a five- or six-month delay because they had been so badly abused in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did Muslims and Croats apply to you? Did they come to you in Pale and say, We want to work?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now look at P7587. We need page two in both versions. Let us just see what kind of document this is. It's dated 2nd July 1995, RDB, the state security sector of the Ministry of Interior of Republika Srpska, sent to the deputy minister of the interior and the public security sector of Bijeljina to the chief in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: One paragraph was put to you from the second page in both versions, so let's move to the second page, paragraph 2 in B/C/S, and paragraph 3 in English. The discussion was about whether it was possible to get information directly from these people or information was derived by surveillance and interception.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here based on comments made by two Muslims, it can be concluded it's probably a conversation that was caught by ham radio operators.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. In the last third of that paragraph, it says: "One of the collocutors who is abroad, advised his friend," does this indicate surveillance or a direct interview with you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, they did not talk to us. We didn't have such communication. All that we caught from Sarajevo were intercepted communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us look briefly at P7025. You were asked, regarding this document, if you were listening or watching Studio B. You said it was a local radio station and then the suggestion was that Belgrade was dozens of kilometres away from you. How far is Belgrade from the place where you were working in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 350 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were you able, ever, to follow Studio B from Pale?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even with their current equipment, Studio B covers only a few municipalities in Belgrade. It's a city station.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see P3355.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Your microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can see here that the Ministry of Interior of Republika Srpska, the office of the minister, on 23rd September 1996 is sending to the minister of justice and administration, Mr. Goran Neskovic, the following report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's see the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do we have a full translation in English? Especially for the first page. Could we go back for a second. B/C/S as well, please. I see some kind of a title below where it says Ministry of Justice and administration, Mr. Goran Neskovic. Then I see something which looks like "predmet."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You are right, Your Honour, this line is missing from the English version. I can read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would briefly read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. It says -- I'll read in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Reference information, submitted to."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the top of the page, the first paragraph in this document, it says: "When Muslim forces made a breakthrough from Srebrenica last year along the Buljim, Konjevic Polje, Cerska, Kamenica, Baljkovici stretch, there were several individual and mass killings among the Muslims. These killings were organised by senior officers so that the chaos in one part of the column would draw the attention and combat activities of the VRS to that part of the column. Thus, the Muslim side created more favourable conditions for the breakthrough of the front part of the column where most military and civilian municipal leaders were."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And can we see the last page of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You remember this document, Mr. Kijac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm going to show you another document and then I'm going to put a question to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need 65 ter number 4079.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the document, let me ask you: Did you have any knowledge about what was happening in Srebrenica? What kind of knowledge did you have? What kind of knowledge did you not have?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all our knowledge is contained in the dispatches, as regards what operatives wrote and what reached me, I mean, I don't know what period you're referring to now but we were following what was happening in Srebrenica through two operatives who were in the area of Srebrenica in the period between, say, the 8th, 9th until, say, 15th or 16th, until the column went through. Because basically we were interested only in the column as regards Srebrenica, because the column could inflict a great deal of harm if it had moved in a different direction through certain villages, Serb villages and you can see this on the basis of our dispatches that most of our operative efforts were in that sense. That was our main work to collect intelligence as to where the column would pass. So that our forces could adapt to that situation in that sense. I don't know what knowledge you mean, I mean, what other knowledge you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was put to you was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I first seek clarification in the report we saw before this one, reference was made to the 280th IBLB and it is suggested to us, although with a question mark, that that would stand for the Eastern Bosnia Light Battalion. First of all, is that your understanding as well of the 280th IBLB.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably. I don't know. I don't know these military formulations. I know that the 28th Division operated there, and I mean, I don't know. I don't know these names, but I assume that that could be that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I then take it that it's a reference to a unit not of the VRS but of the opposing forces?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, could you please --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Context. Context, in what context is it mentioned? I don't have that paper before me. I cannot see where it is mentioned, so I cannot give you an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could we go back to P3355, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Second page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The first large paragraph, a few lines from the bottom, reference is made to the 280th IBLB and its commanding officer, Ibrahim Mandzic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, that's it. I cannot confirm that because this was written by state security, and we just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you don't have to explain why you do not know something. If you don't know, just tell us. That's sufficient. Do the parties agree that this is a unit not of the VRS but from Bosnian forces, if it exists.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, it is a reference to what the document believes is a Muslim force.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed. And perhaps we then move again to the next document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. We should move to 65 ter number 4079, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just say the number again, please, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's 4079. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the 14th of July, 1995 -- your name is typed down there as if you had type-signed this document. But, I mean, since it's a telegram, there is no signature. It says here: "We have information that in the general area of Pobudje, Bratunac municipality, a large Muslim group (reports mention a figure of 5.000 of whom 500 are armed) which is still present is allegedly planning during the coming night a breakthrough through the Milici-Konjevic Polje-Drinjaca road in an attempt to advance towards Tuzla." Is that the column that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, one of the columns. Later on -- I mean, there were several columns. Up until the 16th, until reaching territory that was controlled by the 2nd Muslim Corps, these columns met up and I think that in the evening or afternoon of the 16th, they crossed over. Because there were several columns. There were several leaders, several units, that were independently trying to get out of the siege, and then most of them linked up on the afternoon of the 16th and then they managed to cross over to the area held by the Tuzla Corps, the 2nd corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We tender this document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 04079 receives exhibit number D1350.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1350 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you more about what you knew in relation to developments concerning Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We need 65 ter 4075.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi.
