utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd ask that the witness take his headphones off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, do you understand the English language? Witness? Witness, one second, please. One -- one second. Do you understand or speak the English language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you then take your earphones off.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just to avoid being overtaken by the process of the question and answer and to lay down a marker at this time, I'd ask that Mr. Lukic elicit a basis of knowledge for this document and the date contained in it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, we'll hear whether you follow the suggestion made by Mr. Traldi. Could you put your earphones on again. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This document or the previous one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, this document, which is now on our screen, or the previous one?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The current one. I had no objection as to the previous one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see the bottom part of the document in both versions, please. More, more, more, please, in B/C/S. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague would like to ask you where you received your information from regarding information contained in this document. We see that you signed the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that -- or was it more -- whether the witness knows where this document comes from.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If he could just take the headphones off again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you take off your headphones again for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Because my understanding of his claim in his statement is that he was out of the country at the time this was issued. I'm asking for a basis of knowledge as to the information contained in it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the information contained in it, not for his knowledge of the document itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: For provenance, right but yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please explore whether the witness is familiar with this document, whether he was the one who takes responsibility for the content. His name is under it. And then, after that, what the basis of his knowledge for the content is. Perhaps we do that now and then take a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please put your headphones on again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we go up now and -- yeah, in English version first page, and in B/C/S see the top of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document is dated 16th of July, 1995. You are mentioned further down as the signatory. At this point in time, where were you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Budva. I was in Budva, attending my deputy's wedding, I think from the 14th to 18th. So I am the signatory because that's the way it has to be. However, it's the head of the department that deals with this that actually signed it but he had to sign my name. But I was not in the territory of Republika Srpska. I was in Montenegro attending my deputy's wedding from the 14th until 18th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So in this document, there is a reference to the morning hours of the 16th of July, 1995. Fighting started with Muslim soldiers, at their main part surrounded by the group of Muslim soldiers located west of the Caparde-Zvornik road. Since --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggested some questions to you and you dealt with one of them but not with the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, I have to present what is in the document to ask if the witness knows about the content.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. The first -- I suggested a few other questions. Witness, this document which bears your name, have you seen it at the time that it was sent; that is, the 16th of July?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When have you become familiar with this document, if at all.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, my practice was usually, once I'd returned from the field, I would familiarize myself with documents that were sent to the Main Staff and the president of the republic or, rather, such information that was created on the basis of this kind of information. As for this particular document, I cannot say whether I read it or not, but I certainly read it when I was preparing to testify in the Karadzic case. Now, whether, on that day, the 19th or 20th, whether I read it then, that is what I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic -- no. We take a break. I have -- because you now go to the content and -- We take a break, and we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No speaking aloud, Mr. Mladic, again. We take a break and we resume at 20 minutes past midday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, it happened a few times recently that if you present a 92 bis witness that the Prosecution and I think we more or less have always invited the parties to do so, to add some portions of, for example, the testimony of that witness in another case. If we don't hear any objections to that, we consider this to be accepted. Well, it happened now and then.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know which witness do you have in mind? In general. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In general. It happened, I think, at least two times recently.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It has, Your Honour. And I can think of one occasion where the Defence didn't object -- or didn't accept and did a filing to reflect that they were withdrawing the motion as a result and in the other occasions I don't recall that they've done any filings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So if there's no specific answer to such an additional request, then the Chamber -- or -- is -- always inclined to extend the portion of the testimony in accordance with what the Prosecution has requested. I just wanted to make that clear on the record, that that's how we procedurally proceed in those cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We would offer this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 04075 receives exhibit number D1351, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have 1D06118 on our screens, please. Can we have top of the page enlarged, please, first.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is from RDB, state security sector, Sarajevo, sent to the deputy minister of the interior in person, the CRDB Banja Luka, and the public security chief in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we see the bottom of the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see your signature? These are the correct pages. So, second paragraph from the bottom, in page -- on page 1 in B/C/S and the second paragraph from the bottom as well on page 2 in English. We've seen that the document is dated 14 August 1995, and in this paragraph, we read: "Another two groups of Muslim soldiers from Zepa and Srebrenica were neutralised on 13 August." What was your information, until when did fighting continue with those straggler groups from Srebrenica and Zepa who were trying to break out?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Almost the whole year. My signature is at the bottom but you see that this paper is actually sent to me. If you can go back to the first page. Do you see "the chief of RDB in person." At that time I was in Banja Luka. So from the head office to inform me about a situation on the ground is sent to me in person. At that time I was in Banja Luka because of the well-known situation in Krajina. So this is one of my subordinates who was at that time in the head office at Pale dealing with those problems, and I remember several similar dispatches referring to groups of soldiers who, after the fall of Srebrenica, were moving through that area, because it's a huge area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would offer this one into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 1D06118 receives exhibit number D1352.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you deal with Srebrenica before July 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did. Srebrenica was a subject of our interest from the outbreak of the war, and it was within the jurisdiction of our detachment in Zvornik, our operative section in Zvornik, which covered that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see 1D6116. We don't have the translation of this document, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So I will read out what it's about. We see at the top MUP of Republika Srpska, RDB state security sector, Sarajevo. On 28th June 1995, it was sent to the deputy minister of the interior of Republika Srpska in person and the chief of the RDB in person. In the third paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, was it to the chief of RDB or RJB.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... RJB. I said RJB.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, you misspoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we see that third paragraph. It says: "The units of the so-called BH army, around 500 hours on 28 June 1995 attacked VRS positions at Tuk and Cecavka." What did you say?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing, nothing. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "Ten fighters were wounded and, at the same time, there was an attack at Jasen in the area of responsibility of the 3rd SPB." And in the last sentence, it says: "In parallel with the infantry attacks, the enemy shelled civilian targets as well." And let's look at the second page. It says: "In a sabotage terrorist action carried out by Muslim units in the area of Han Pijesak municipality on 27 June this year, one of the groups, according to available information, was led by Avdo Palic himself." A bit further below, it says: "In his report to the higher command, Palic stated that in that action 40 Serb soldiers were killed, several dozens were wounded, and one was taken prisoner." What kind of reports did you get before the operation against Srebrenica? What were the actions of the Muslim forces from Srebrenica and Zepa?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime in mid-June, and even before, we had operative information, that is to say, intelligence, about a high concentration of Muslim forces in the area of Sarajevo and that a breakout operation from Sarajevo was being prepared. Except the 7th and the 5th Corps, all corps provided their numerical strength. Even those from Srebrenica. We got reports that units from Srebrenica, including sabotage groups, were being pulled out of Srebrenica and moving towards Sarajevo, preparing for that action to cut off the western part of Sarajevo, and this indicates that, at the same time, on -- at the same time, the 28th Division was given the task to launch surprise attacks against our forces in that area so that we, that is to say, the Army of Republika Srpska, would not be able to send part of our forces from that area to Sarajevo. You've shown me only one or two reports, but I believe there are more, describing actions launched from the protected areas in order to bind our forces and to prevent them from sending reinforcement to Sarajevo in which a fierce offensive by Muslim forces was underway.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kijac. We would like to tender this document. And I would like to show only one more document and conclude with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 1D06116 receives exhibit number D1353, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Should be marked for identification because there's no translation. Therefore, D1353 is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have on our screens P01677, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kijac, this document was shown to you earlier today. It's a document from the Main Staff of the VRS granting approval for travel to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and we see a list of four persons. The first is Drazen Erdemovic. We see the approval was given. Drazen Erdemovic is travelling under his true name. Would this approval be valid if he had carried documents with a different name? Would it be able -- would it have been possible to compare it at the border?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wouldn't have been. Because if Erdemovic had received our documents he wouldn't know in which name it would be. We issue IDs with certain names, and we register them in a log-book, and only if there occurs a problem and we cannot find out who is carrying that document, then we pull out that log-book and we see on whose request - not to which person, only on whose request - a new identity was given to someone. So this is a bit strange because we see that it was on the 11th February 1996, and we had issued that paper, according to the other document, in January on that year. We did issue papers, but we don't know to whom.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So Drazen Erdemovic could use this certificate only on his true name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he could cross the border only as Drazen Erdemovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kijac. That's all the we had for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Traldi, any further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just very briefly, Your Honour. Can we have 65 ter 20742.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And as it comes up at temporary transcript page 38, Mr. Lukic asked you about pre-war negotiations and you said Mr. Zulfikarpasic had made an initiative that Bosnia remain whole. That was in the summer of 1991; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was before the war.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please speak into the microphone, Witness, and could you repeat what you said. And the question was whether it was in the summer of 1991.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I couldn't say now whether it was the summer, but it was certainly before the outbreak of the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is an intercepted conversation involving Momcilo Mandic and several different interlocutors dated the 5th of May, 1992. You're aware of Mr. Mandic; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to page 10 in the English and the middle of page 11 in the B/C/S. Ten in the English at the very bottom, read Mandic is speaking with Bruno Stojic, one of the authorities in Herceg-Bosna about the Neretva river, and he says: "The left bank to the Serbs, the right bank to the Croats, the Muslims can go down the river." By the beginning of May 1992, there was no longer any possibility of Bosnia remaining whole; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It all depended on the international community and agreement between parties. There is always a hypothetical possibility for the war to be stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And what Mr. Mandic is saying here is that in part of Bosnia and Herzegovina there was no place for Muslims; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN KIJAC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see a sentence here of Mr. Mandic's and it does remind me of Mr. Mandic. If you allow me, I will read it out. "Don't be kidding. Well, you have to let us bathe a bit." Well, that's the relationship. They were both assistant ministers in 1991 when there was this tripartite government. Bruno Stojic was the assistant minister for material and technical affairs and Mr. Mandic was assistant minister for crime prevention.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I tender this intercept, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 20742 receives exhibit number P7663, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do we need all 29 pages, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think all 29 pages are relevant, and in similar conversations, and between Herceg-Bosna and RS authorities about division. We had this, I think it's with P6727, The Koljevic-Tudjman meeting, where the parties spoke about it for a while and then decide the whole thing should be in. I'd exceptionally suggest the same approach be taken here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's accepted. P7663 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That completes my questions for the witness, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since the Bench also has no further questions for you, Mr. Kijac, this concludes your testimony. I'd like to thank you very much for coming a long way to The Hague and for - even twice - and for having answered the questions that were put to you by the parties and that were put to you by the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the Defence ready to call its next witness, which would be Mr. Kovac if I am well-informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You are well-informed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there was another matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I was reminded by your staff that I should read something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, would you please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During the testimony of Mr. Kijac, Dragan on 19th October 2015, Exhibits D01294 and D01295 were marked for identification pending an English translation to be uploaded. We can find on transcript pages 39977 up to 39990. English translation for these exhibits were uploaded into e-court under doc IDs 1D26-3910 and 1D26-3911. So the Defence will request that the Court Officer be instructed to attach to the original and for its admission into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, you are hereby instructed to attach the documents of which the numbers were read - and we checked that on the transcript - appear correctly on the transcript to D1294 and D1295 and both are admitted into evidence. If there's any concern about the translation, the Prosecution has, as always, an opportunity to revisit the matter within the next 48 hours. Mr. Traldi, anything you'd like to have the attention of Mr. Lukic as well, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I was waiting to allow him to consult. I had actually been reminded of a similar matter by Chambers staff, and can't allow Mr. Lukic to be more diligent than I am so I have one very related matter to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A similar matter. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The Prosecution has received an English translation for P7590 MFI, 65 ter 33169, which was marked for identification through Witness Kijac on 22nd of October 2015, pending a translation. The translation has been uploaded into e-court under doc ID 0678-4510-BCST which makes me think it might have been a B/C/S translation we received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you wanted --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If the Defence have no objection, we ask that be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar, you're hereby instructed to attach the document just referred to by Mr. Traldi which appears on the transcript to P7590. P7590 is admitted into evidence, and as always, 48 hours to revisit the matter if need be. Good afternoon, Mr. Kovac. First of all, our apologies for dealing with other matters when you entered the courtroom. Before you give evidence, the rules require that you make a solemn declaration, the text of which is now handed out to you. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Kovac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kovac, you'll first be examined by Mr. Ivetic. You find Mr. Ivetic to your left. Mr. Ivetic is a member of the Defence team of Mr. Mladic. Mr. Ivetic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It would be more convenient if you put your earphones from the top of your head and not from the back.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day, General.

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you please state your full name, first and last, for of the purposes of the record.

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: Mitar Kovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would like to first call up your curriculum vitae, 1D6015, in e-court. I also have a hard copy in Serbian which, with the assistance of the usher and after Prosecution counsel has looked at it, I would ask to be given to the witness. And my first question, sir, is: Have you had a chance to review this document in full prior to today?

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I did have an opportunity.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And is your CV up to date, or does it need to be updated with additional information?

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: Well, there are some elements pertaining to the last two years that have not been included.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we look at page 1 in both versions, your current post since January 2013 is listed as chief of the strategic planning administration, Ministry of Defence, Republic of Serbia. What, if anything, do we need to add here to bring this CV current?

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: It is necessary to add that on the 22nd of December, 2014, at my own request, I was retired from the mentioned position.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And apart from retiring from the mentioned position within the Ministry of Defence, has that retirement affected your other positions, such as the research or teaching positions, listed later on in your CV?

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: No. On the contrary. I've already said that I retired at my own request, precisely for the purpose of devoting myself to scientific research. What I did throughout my career so I remained there at the war college for officers' training for doctoral thesis and so on. And also I work with several schools of the University of Belgrade and also with a private university.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I see, sir, up to 1991 you had various commands in army units and I'd like to ask you about the time-period between 1991 and 2004 while you were at the institute. Did you have occasion to be assigned anywhere to combat units?

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: As I arrived in the institute in 1991, certain units became involved in the theatre of war so at the end of November 1991, I was sent to the JNA units that were in the theatre of war in the Republic of Croatia where I was commander of an artillery battalion for six months. I did not give back the post that I had held until then. That is to say that this was a temporary assignment. After that I returned to the same post that I held at the institute of the art of war. And then at the end of January 1993, I was temporarily assigned yet again to be at the Herzegovina Corps of the Army of Republika Srpska --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We missed the exact post. The witness is speaking too fast.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After these six months --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, the translators said that they missed the exact post that you had in the Herzegovina Corps and they've asked that you try to speak slower. So if you could repeat your answer beginning right after your assignment to the Herzegovina Corps of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: At the end of January 1993, I was temporarily reassigned to the Herzegovina Corps and it was Chief of Staff of the artillery regiment. That was the post I held until the beginning of August 1993. And I returned to the institute of the art of war yet again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And could you tell us, apart from that which we have just gone through, is the rest of your CV complete and up to date?

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: I think that the rest of my CV has remained unchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Then I'd like to focus a bit on the part of your CV that lists your scientific research and teaching career. This is on the bottom of page 1 in English and it is on the top of page 2 in the Serbian. So I'd ask that we go to page 2 in the Serbian version and, of course, you have a hard copy in front of you. I'd like to ask you, first, in relation to your time at the Strategic Research Institute, if you could tell us what kinds of topics or subjects were covered by your work there.

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: The institute of the -- of strategic research and before that, the art of war institute, was an institution of the JNA that dealt in research pertaining to art of war --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: I do apologise. I do apologise. As a young officer, I started working at that institute, that is to say in 1991, and when I was sent to JNA units in the theatre of war in the Republic of Croatia, I carried out part of a project that had to do with the activity the JNA units in crisis areas during the civil war in the SFRY. Gradually I developed as a researcher, and gradually I attained all levels from researcher to scientific advisor in 2004. As a scientific advisor and as a senior scientific associate, I was the leader of several significant projects in that institute.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can now turn the page in the English version and stay on the same page in the Serbian version, we see here a reference to both the Military Academy and the University of Defence in this same section. Could you tell us what subjects or topics or themes were the focus of your activities at these institutions.

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: At the academy and later on at the University of Defence, I taught primarily at doctoral studies, masters studies, in the field of strategy, military strategy, strategic management, strategic planning, programming, and the system of planning, programming, budgeting and execution.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you've mentioned earlier and here we have listed two faculties at Belgrade university, the faculty of security and the faculty of political science, can you tell us precisely what your positions at these faculties entailed.

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: At the faculty of security for a rather long period of time, about five years, I taught at the level of masters studies and doctoral studies in the field of defence systems and at the faculty of political science, the primary subject had to do with the strategy of national security, the strategy of defence, security challenges and threats from global to national levels.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, in relation to the areas of research and professional focus and it is towards the bottom of the page in English but we have to go to the next page of your CV that is page 3 in the Serbian --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic [sic], before we continue, is this the same version we have before us as the one that was submitted earlier? Or is it a new one or ... because the text seems to be not exactly the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would have to check on that, Your Honours. It's the only CV I know of, so I would imagine ... that it ought to be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the headings of the one we have seen, for example, if we look at research area and professional focus, the version we have says research area and professional focus, whereas the one we are looking at now says areas of research and professional focus. Under -- so at least the text is not the same. So -- and then, of course, we could go through it and find out what is different. But it seems that there are two versions. The one which you submitted earlier, and now the one we have on our screen, and I think they both come from you, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Without knowing which one you have in front of you, I can't say with certainty but it could be a translation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What we have in front of us is the one you asked to be on our screens. I mean, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes. And I don't have access to the other one that you have in front of you that you say is different, therefore I can't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... submitted, which has the numbers of filing on top it. That's, of course, the ones you have submitted earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And that's why I suggest I look at that during the break since I'm ill prepared to address that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We see it one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In my view it was attached to defence notice of disclosure of expert report filed 16 February 2015. This is the hard copy we have in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It may be and I will check to see whether this is an updated version or an updated translation, perhaps. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We are comparing the English. Only the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, and the English would be a translation, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but apparently then you provided two different translations. I mean, I don't know where you got them from, but it's your responsibility, whatever you submit, and we're now looking at a document we prepared for the other one and we noticed that they're not the same. And I have one additional question in this context for the witness. Witness, you told us that your CV didn't cover the last two years, or at least the last two years since 2013 were not reflected. What caused that, that you have not dealt with the last two years? Could you tell us why the last two years are not in your CV as it was presented to us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I said at the beginning that the only essential difference is in my retirement. All the other elements of my biography are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't ask you what is the difference. I asked you why the last two years, if that includes your retirement, fine, why the last two years are not to be found in your CV, as it was presented to us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I arrived here, I communicated that change in my professional career. Before that, I did not have any opportunity to make a change in my CV.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the previous one, was that prepared for another case or ... your previous CV.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, that earlier CV I submitted together with my expert report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ivetic, if years are missing and if the witness draws your attention to that, rather than to ask him to explain all that in court it would have been better that a revised CV and then preferably one where there exists only one version to be presented. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may. With multiple Prosecution witnesses they've walked in with updated CVs and it's been the practice in this courtroom to update them because time sometimes passes between when the materials are filed and when the witness comes to testify. So quite frankly, I'm a little surprised by Your Honours' instruction now with relation to just bringing current a CV for two years since the report was drafted. I don't understand why this is becoming such an issue when with Prosecution witnesses it was not an issue. I'm frankly quite concerned about the manner in which this witness is being treated by this Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not treating this witness at this moment. The CV presented is dated, initially presented, is dated Belgrade, 2013. The only thing I am --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The problem, Mr. Ivetic, is that under the document number 1D06015, we obviously have two different versions. This is a problem. That was listed in your list of Defence exhibits as CV of this witness, but you submitted, with your Defence notice, another version of the CV. That is the problem. And it's obviously the same number. That has to be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And that will be clarified, but again, I note Ewa Tabeau, expert witness of the Prosecution had a second CV. I believe Mr. Dannatt had a second CV. It's a situation that has come up before and so I'm quite surprised to be getting the responses that I'm getting that we need to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I would not have dealt with it if you would not have presented two different CVs under the same number to this Chamber, where we have to find out that there are two versions without any further explanation. I would not have dealt with the other matter if this would not have triggered it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now that the translation is completed --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, in relation to areas of research and professional focus, that is towards the bottom of the page in the English and is now at the top of the page in the Serbian version, the sixth entry lists co-operation with NATO within the framework of the DRG, the Defence Research Group. Can you tell us a bit more about what your work in this regard entailed.

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: With my appointment to the head of administration in this group in the Ministry of Defence which is in the defence sector, I co-operated ex officio with representatives of NATO, primarily with the sector for the planning of forces and defence policy, and through that co-operation, this DRG group was established. It was the instrument for co-operation between member states of NATO and the Republic of Serbia and its Ministry of Defence. I can say that this co-operation is ongoing. It continues through various mechanisms, including meetings, and various groups that have been established to deal with a variety of issues covered by the defence ministry and the Army of Yugoslavia -- and the Army of Serbia, beginning with charting of policies and the establishment of forces to work under the UN mandate.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And could you provide us a few more details about the subject matter of that work when you say, "policies and establishment of forces within the Army of Serbia." What precisely was the type of tasks that were being analysed and worked upon by way of this co-operative group with NATO?

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: Groups were formed following the principle of work tables. Every work table had several functions falling within the defence system. The most active were four work tables. One was for defence policy; and second for the preparation of army units and army units reform; the third for logistics within the defence system; and the fourth security and intelligence sector. Now, I don't know if it's necessary to speak about these various sectors in detail. Essentially, every work table included co-operation with several NATO member states and the partnership for peace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I don't think we need any more details beyond what you've given but I would like to know the time-period that you participated in such workings with the DRG group and NATO. What time-period during your career in terms of years?

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: From 2007 until I retired in 2014; that is to say, seven years. I had a position in the defence ministry, then became head of the administration for technical planning, and then head of administration for planning and development in the General Staff of the Army of Serbia where I spent three years.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now, sir, I'd like to take a moment looking at the listing of publications which is to be found on page 4 in both English and Serbian. And the first question I have for you, sir: Are these all the books, monographs and publications that you have published during your career?

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: There should be a sentence saying that this is only an excerpt of all the papers and books that I published during my research scientific and professional career. Monographs are all there. Studies, only partially. And as for articles, there are just a few listed because I published more than 100 in domestic and foreign magazines.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to focus on just a few items we see here. We see in the second and third items under books, "History of the Art of War." And we see under item number 2 of the research projects - which will be on the next page in the Serbian - the same title with the dates 1995 to 2000. What exactly is this publication?

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: It was a fundamental research project designed by the institute for the art of war, and on average, eight researchers were involved. This fundamental research was done for educational and scientific and research motives because it was estimated that there was a need for the -- for monographs to be published at the end of that research, that is to say, publications that could be used in education, in the education of officers and cadets in the Military Academy. The purpose of this project has been accomplished in full, and to the great joy of the authors of this monograph, it has been used with great success in teaching.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have a question for clarification. Sir, what is the substantive difference between these two publications. One is "History of Art of War," the other one is "History of Military Art"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this part under the subheading "Studies and monographs," is the entirety of the project which includes all the methodological aspects of the project beginning with the development of the concept, the observation of all the elements required for the manufacturing of instruments, developments of plans and engagement, and this period was two years before research itself began. The connection between these two subheadings, between these two titles is spans a period of time in which three monographs were published that fall within one volume of "The History of the Art of War" that is the essential connection. The -- as the output of the project, these monographs and books were published.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I probably didn't express myself very clearly. My question was: What is the substantive difference between "The History of Art of War," and "History of Military Art"? Although the headings are slightly different, they seem to connote to me the same kind of topic, and I'm just trying to find out if, indeed, they deal with two different areas and what is that difference?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the same field. But, first of all, comes the research procedure and, at the end of the process, are the monographs listed here. It's the same field of science: The art of war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The reason I'm asking is because in item 3, it covers the period 1920 to 2000 and the other one, "The History of Military Art" covers 1995 to 2000; and if it's the same field, it looks like 1995 to 2000 is a duplication of what is already contained in "The History of Art of War."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do not see 1995 up till 200 anywhere. Maybe that's a mistranslation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Maybe we are looking at two different reports now that we realise there are two different reports. The hard copy I have before me, under management and participation in managing scientific research projects, item 2 says: "History of Military Art, 1995 to 2000."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And you have it in front of you on the screen in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's not the way it is here in the printed version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we are dealing with different versions of the CV, perhaps. Mr. Ivetic, since you will pay attention to that matter anyhow during the next break perhaps you could also look at this aspect of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can. I can already note that number 2 on the screen has "History of the Art of War," but that is in the "Lead researcher and research projects" and I think that seems to be what Your Honour is asking about, since I don't see any reference to 1995 through 2000 under the books.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, it's not under the books.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] It's not under the books. As I indicated, it's under the heading, "Management and participating in managing in scientific research projects." That's the heading I have on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And that's bottom of the page in the English on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Your microphone was off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Apparently my microphone was off. I was saying this one is under the heading, "Management and participation in managing in scientific research projects," and it's item 2, under that heading which says "History of military art (1995 to 2000)." And I think my colleague is quoting from the written version and on the screen we see "Lead researcher and researcher in scientific projects." Again, that's not exactly the same text, where under 2 we find "The History of the Art of War (1995-2000)." So, again, in order to find the right places, we have to carefully compare the various English versions of this. But that's what apparently Judge Moloto focussed on that. Could you perhaps look at that as well during the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kovac, we'll take a break. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll take a break, and we'll resume at quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the witness to be escorted into the courtroom, Mr. Ivetic, could you further inform the Chamber about the versions, at least in the English language of the CV.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can. During the break I have confirmed that the B/C/S version attached to the motion filed on the 15th of February and the one in e-court are the exact same. What is at issue are the translations of the English. The one that was attached to the motion is a draft translation that was prepared at the behest of OLAD when seeking appointment of this witness insofar as the CLSS official translation was not ready at that time. The CLSS official translation only was completed a few days before the filing of the 94 bis notice for this witness and somehow the old CV was copied onto that filing. We've checked the text of the two and the main difference comes in the inartful translation of the headings and, for instance, the use of the word "the head" instead of "chief," then use of the word "multiple" instead of "numerous" articles, and as Judge Moloto pointed out the inartful number 2 under lead researcher items where it's "The History of the Art of War" in both the B/C/S original and the CLSS translation, and the draft translation had the words transposed in the manner that we discussed before the break. I apologise for any confusion caused by that since I only knew of one B/C/S original, that is why I was confused by the existence of differences, where now we know where they come from and, again, the version in e-court if we scroll down can be even seen as the CLSS official translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Judge Moloto has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do I understand, then, that the one that we are going to be using during this witness's testimony is the one that's on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, in response to one of my observations, Mr. Ivetic, you said that we treated the Defence different from the Prosecution. I tried to just find out about updated CVs in relation to Tabeau, and I think twice even, in relation to Mr. Donia, in relation to Witness Brunborg, I think also in relation to Witness Haglund. There are always written new versions of the CV, and when there was only a verbal update in relation to Witness Radovanovic. The Chamber didn't make that much of a fuss about that. We were -- well, without any comment, it was done. So I don't know whether you wanted to refer that I was -- blaming the Chamber for accepting updates from the Prosecution and not accepting updates from the Defence or - and that's what I had on my mind - is to have uploaded an updated CV and I see -- I may not have checked all of them but most of the expert witnesses of the Prosecution if there was an updated CV it was presented in written form and that's what I thought I would encourage the Defence to do the same, and that was all triggered by the fact that there were even several English versions, two different English versions of the CV. Let's move on. Let's leave all this behind us and let's focus on what we're here for, that is, to hear the evidence of this witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: General, sir, I'd like to follow up some more on the publication the "History of the Art of War," and I'd like to ask you how it has been received within the industry since being published?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Objection. Vague. It's not really clear. Industry? What industry? What are we talking about? The relevance of the question is also not exactly clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me first check. Do you understand the question, what Mr. Ivetic is asking you, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What -- how do you understand "the industry," what that means in this context?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My understanding is that this meant being leader of a project because I really did lead that project in the second half. And that is something that was discussed a moment ago and that is written here. The result of this project are these three books, out of which two were mentioned in the part that pertains to books. Numbers 2 and 3. And the only thing missing here is the "History of Serbian Art of War." So this is three volumes. And all three were well received. I understand that that was the question, how they were received. All three were well received and -- oh, okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the question was mainly received well by whom? Because Mr. Weber and the same is true for me, by the way, was not clearly clear yet whether was meant by "the industry" which received your books well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My understanding was that the question was how they were received in military practice and the school system. That is to say, how they were received by the readers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Although --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that is how you understood the question and if Mr. Ivetic wanted to ask you this, then I think you've answered the question, that they were received well and we now also know by whom. Next question, please, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is that work, "The Art of War," a Serbian-only publication or is it available in other languages?

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: First, it was published in Serbian and then in English and it's used in the exchange of literature with universities of defence of other countries with which the University of Defence has co-operation. There are a few proposals and requests to have this translated into the national languages of these academies, and, as far as I know, talks are underway right now. That's what the publisher said.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And has this or any other publication that you have authored received any awards?

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: This publication did receive a reward at the book fair in Nis. The name of the award is Transplantation of Wisdom. Also there is an article about functions of combat that was rewarded in 1997. This is a reward from Vojno Delo. It was called the 22nd of December. And it was the top reward in the then-Yugoslav army.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And earlier before the break you mentioned foreign publications. In which countries have some of your publications been published?

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: Mostly in the recent past, when we've established co-operation with other scientific institutions in the world and when we had opportunity to attend international meetings and publish articles. For now, a part of my monograph was published in a very prestigious magazine in the UK, in India, in Austria in a national magazine dealing with national security and defence and in some other countries.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just one last item that I'd like to look at, and that's item number 7 under your publications, and it is entitled: Determining the effectiveness of systems of military organisation. What can you tell us about this publication?

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: First of all, I led this project at the institute, as you can see in the next chapter, from 2002 to 2004. The result of that project is the monograph published in the military publishing institute. The monograph is a theoretical basis for determining the efficiency of all military organisational systems from the highest to the lowest organisational structures. As such, it introduced a number of novelties in mathematical modelling and the methodology of determining the combat functionality of units. Part of this article was published in a prestigious English magazine. At their request, a smaller part of the article was published at symposium and then this article as a chapter of the monograph was expanded.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And this work that we've just discussed, did it relate to examining only the Serbian army or did it relate to any other armies?

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: Well, it's a scientific research project which is applicable to many armies in the world, and we know that part of that research has been accepted in the US army as well, in the modelling of new instructions for determining the combat value of units. In evaluating combat units, using mathematical models given in this paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Defence would tender 1D06015 into evidence as the next public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It receives exhibit number D1354, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: General, did you prepare an expert report for the instant case, the case we're here for today?

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Prior to this case, the Mladic case, have you ever appeared previously as an expert in any other court proceedings?

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like now to call up 1D05358 in e-court. I don't know if you have a copy. If not, I have a hard copy that I can provide to the usher. While we wait for that, if you could look on the screen, do you recognise the report that is now on our screens?

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And could you tell us when you were first asked to -- I'm sorry, I see counsel rising?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I have no objection to copy of the report that's been handed to me although I do see that the witness has other prepared papers in front of him which I believe to be the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, do you have the report in front of you or is there anything else you have -- could you tell us what is on the desk before you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I only have the report and blank paper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Blank paper, no problem, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No. If there are any markings in the copy in front of him though the Prosecution would like to have the opportunity to see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is your copy marked in any way? Anything added to it? Or is it a clean copy? Well, it's only if -- if it's a clean copy then ... okay. Mr. Weber, you look at it at least at the same time we give the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's an identical copy. Exactly the same as the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was whether there were any annotations on it made by you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: There are some small markings but the Prosecution doesn't have any problem with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So you can use either version of the report you'd prefer. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: General, when you were first asked to prepare an expert report for this case, what precisely was your assignment?

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: My task was to try to write in keeping with the indictment, a military expert report on the civil war in Bosnia-Herzegovina. During my talks with lawyer Nenad Petrusic, I tried to gain an idea about the scope of the work, for what period it is to be done, what material is available for my research and study, and all the other issues that were important to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And could you tell us how you set out to perform your assignment? What types of things did you review?

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: I reviewed various sources, primarily of original material originating from the warring parties in Bosnia-Herzegovina, plans of action, material about various levels of organisation of these armies, plans of warfare, all the planning related to the Sarajevo theatre of war and the protected areas of Srebrenica and Zepa. Along with the primary sources, I also used the published works by authors, leaders, commanders in the Croatian army, in the HVO; in the Muslim army, that is to say, the BH army; as well as the Army of Republika Srpska. The problem that I felt during my entire work on the report was the lack or shortage of documents related to the BH army, the Croatian army, and the Croatian Defence Council. I tried to solve this problem partially by locating documents in monographs that have been published about the war between these armies in this period of the civil war. Also, I used reports or expert reports from the Office of the Prosecutor and from Defence experts in various cases heard before this Tribunal, primarily those written by General Radinovic, and an expert report related to the command and control and the system of command in the Army of Republika Srpska made for the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you mentioned the review of expert reports of Prosecution experts. Which ones?

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: Primarily the Butler and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the other name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Reports in the Krstic case and the Karadzic case, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if you could just repeat after Butler the interpreters did not catch the name of the second name that you used for the Prosecution expert reports that you reviewed?

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: General Dannatt.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in terms of the documentation that was cited in the footnotes of your report, how did you determine what would be used or cited therein?

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: In view of my experience in writing in general, for many paragraphs and chapters, I could name more than one source, but I usually cited the source that was the closest to me at the moment and which covered the greatest number of facts concerning a given qualification.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And out of this wide variety of sources that you consulted, what was the main type of document that you relied upon in reaching your conclusions?

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: For the most part, I relied on documents of command, of different types and different levels of command, reports, studies and monographs, as well as video footage of specific events.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the last question before we get to the break for today, as to the organisation and functioning of the VRS, did you consult any additional sources of information; and, if so, which ones?

utterances.speaker: MITAR KOVAC
utterances.text: As for the functioning of the Army of Republika Srpska, I used reports about the combat readiness of VRS units that were done periodically. I used my personal knowledge and the personal knowledge and personal interviews with various officers who held different positions in the Army of Republika Srpska and I used written sources, monographs or books, that have been published about the VRS in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are at the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we take that break, one very short question: Do you have a list of those officers you interviewed so we would know which your sources are?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Specifically, I talked to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just wondered whether you have listed them somewhere. I'm not asking you at this moment to -- to read or to -- that list but whether you have a list.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know with whom I talked. It's not a great number of people. It's two or three men. And I know, of course, their names and I can tell them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if is just two or three, perhaps you write them down so that if, at any point in time, we or the parties would be interested in it, that you would have them available. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour, we would interested in the names, we would also, if there's any recording or information about the substance that was provided during the interviews, we'd also appreciate that. And just on a related matter, but based on the witness's answer, he made reference to multiple combat readiness reports. We do see that there are a number that are referenced in his report. We have asked the Defence for the ones that we don't have. If there are any that we do not current possess, which I don't think we do possess all of them, if the Defence could please provide them to us today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's not for the witness but it's, rather, for the Defence. Witness, if you could, if it's only two or three names perhaps you mention them now and we don't have to -- we don't have to ask you to write them down, give them to VWS. If you know these two or three names, then please give them now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can tell you right now. I spoke with General Vinko Pandurevic; with General Grubac, commander of a corps; and Colonel Milenko Lalovic, who was battalion commander in Nevesinje Brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear which corps General Grubac was commander of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us which corps you referred to in relation to General Grubac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Herzegovina Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then last, very short question. Have you recorded any of those conversations, either audio or video.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. These interviews were not prepared or official. It was an informal talk where I, as a researcher, tried to check out some of my knowledge, and hear the opinion of people from whom I should try to get some sort of position that I would later evaluate in my own way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I said the last question, but I'm joining in a bad practice, that -- to make my last question not a last question. Did you make any notes of those interviews which would be available?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't. It was not a -- methodologically speaking, a interview. It was informal talk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you relied on your recollection of those conversations, not on any note?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In these specific conversations, yes. Because I was just confirming and evaluating personal views.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. This really was my last question. We'd like to see you back tomorrow. But before you leave this courtroom, I would like to instruct you that you should not speak or communicate with whomever about your testimony, that is testimony given today or testimony still to be given the day or the days to come. If there's clear to you, you may follow the usher --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: One item. Your Honour said tomorrow. I believe you meant next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. Because tomorrow is Friday; we're not sitting. Witness, you even have more than a weekend. We would like to see you on Monday, the 16th of November, rather than tomorrow. Therefore, you may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently, Mr. Ivetic, I always think that a week is longer than it actually is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: As do I sometimes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps that's wishful thinking. We adjourn for the day and we resume Monday, the 16th of November, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 16th day of November, 2015, at 9.30 a.m.
